title: PALO Two-Lens AI Maturity Assessment
methodology: Evidence-bounded ordinal profile; no national ranking, certification or authorization. PALO-designed rubric, not BCG ASPIRE scoring.

levels.label: Absent
levels.description: Evidence records that the capability is absent in scope.

levels.label: Documented
levels.description: Named ownership, boundaries and procedures are documented.

levels.label: Tested
levels.description: A repeatable test demonstrates the capability in the stated scope.

levels.label: Monitored
levels.description: Repeated operational observations and change responses are recorded.

levels.label: Challenged and improved
levels.description: Independent challenge, contrary evidence and verified improvement are recorded.

domains.title: Deployment capability
domains.description: Can this scoped organization or system turn AI plans into working capability?

domains.title: Institutional capability
domains.description: Can accountable people supervise, challenge and correct the system?

domains.title: Delegated authority
domains.description: Who may decide or act, under which limits and revocation conditions?

domains.title: Observable behaviour
domains.description: Can actual behaviour, effects and harms be observed and corrected?

domains.title: Verifiable evidence
domains.description: Can claims be traced, challenged and refreshed over time?

questions.title: Purpose and delivery ownership
questions.prompt: Are intended value, prohibited uses, accountable owners and delivery decisions explicit?
questions.evidence: Approved purpose and delivery record, delivery review and outcome sample.
questions.action: Assign a delivery owner and verify intended value against a scoped pilot.

questions.title: Practical skills
questions.prompt: Can operators, engineers and reviewers demonstrate the skills needed for their roles?
questions.evidence: Role competence matrix, observed tasks and refresher results.
questions.action: Test role competence with realistic tasks, then close the observed gaps.

questions.title: Data and infrastructure
questions.prompt: Are data, compute, access and recovery available at the required quality and scale?
questions.evidence: Data fitness results, capacity measurements and restore tests.
questions.action: Validate data fitness, capacity and recovery against the intended operating envelope.

questions.title: Sustainable delivery resources
questions.prompt: Can the team fund and operate the capability over its intended lifecycle?
questions.evidence: Operating budget, support ownership and measured service capacity.
questions.action: Document lifecycle cost and staffed operational capacity.

questions.title: Evaluation and improvement
questions.prompt: Can the team validate performance and introduce improvements reproducibly?
questions.evidence: Versioned evaluation set, release comparison and failed-test records.
questions.action: Define representative evaluations and a repeatable release review.

questions.title: Dependency resilience
questions.prompt: Can the organization continue or exit when a model, supplier or infrastructure dependency changes?
questions.evidence: Dependency map, portability exercise and exit or continuity test.
questions.action: Exercise an exit or continuity scenario for a material dependency.

questions.title: Accountable oversight
questions.prompt: Do named reviewers have the authority, time and competence to intervene?
questions.evidence: Mandate, reviewer competence test and intervention record.
questions.action: Name the accountable reviewer and test an intervention under realistic conditions.

questions.title: Independent challenge
questions.prompt: Can reviewers challenge a deployment decision and track corrective action without conflicts of interest?
questions.evidence: Challenge minutes, conflict declaration and closed corrective-action sample.
questions.action: Run a challenge session and assign independently reviewed corrective actions.

questions.title: Affected people and remedy
questions.prompt: Can affected people understand an outcome, contest it and obtain a reasoned remedy?
questions.evidence: Accessible notice, appeal journey, independent review and verified closure sample.
questions.action: Test the notice, appeal and remedy journey with representative affected people.

questions.title: Dependency and policy accountability
questions.prompt: Are supplier commitments and policy changes reviewed for relevance with an owner and deadline?
questions.evidence: Versioned supplier terms, PolicyWatcher or other source observation, human applicability decision and exit owner.
questions.action: Review one material supplier or policy change and record its scoped control impact.

questions.title: Explicit decision boundaries
questions.prompt: Are permitted and prohibited decisions, resources, data uses and delegation limits explicit?
questions.evidence: Authority mandate, Action Claim or equivalent scoped decision record and negative tests.
questions.action: Document and test authority boundaries, including advisory-only limits.

questions.title: Approval and separation of duties
questions.prompt: Are consequential decisions tied to a specific current request and authorized independent review?
questions.evidence: Approval-to-request binding, role separation and stale-approval rejection test.
questions.action: Bind approvals to exact requests and test unauthorized or stale reuse.

questions.title: Revocation and containment
questions.prompt: Can humans stop or restrict the system and demonstrate that revoked authority no longer works?
questions.evidence: Revocation drill, denial records and authoritative stop observation.
questions.action: Test revocation, containment and any remaining direct execution paths.

questions.title: Change and delegation continuity
questions.prompt: Do model, prompt, memory, tool and subagent changes trigger review of inherited authority?
questions.evidence: Version-bound change review, delegation chain and regression evidence.
questions.action: Reassess authority after a representative model, memory, tool or delegation change.

questions.title: Observed effects
questions.prompt: Can actual effects be checked separately from permission and execution success?
questions.evidence: Decision, execution receipt and authoritative post-state sample; mismatches and missing observations.
questions.action: Test a mismatch and a missing observation as well as a successful effect.

questions.title: Harm and disparity monitoring
questions.prompt: Are failure, unfair outcomes and accessibility barriers measured for affected groups?
questions.evidence: Representative subgroup evaluation, denominator, uncertainty and remediation decision.
questions.action: Evaluate affected groups and document sample limits and residual harms.

questions.title: Incident response and recovery
questions.prompt: Can the team detect, contain, investigate and learn from incidents and near misses?
questions.evidence: Incident exercise, triage timestamps, recovery results and accountable follow-up.
questions.action: Exercise an incident with containment, escalation and verified recovery.

questions.title: Long-term and physical consequences
questions.prompt: Are cumulative exposure, physical effects and resource consumption bounded and reviewed where relevant?
questions.evidence: Scope-specific cumulative limits, physical safety or safe-stop tests, environmental measurement and rationale.
questions.action: Review cumulative effects and resource budgets; explain which physical hazards apply to the scope.

questions.title: Traceable decision chain
questions.prompt: Can a reviewer trace each sampled claim to authority, action, effect and accountable decision?
questions.evidence: Retrievable version-bound decision chain with identity, timestamps and evidence integrity checks.
questions.action: Reconstruct a complete decision chain and record missing links.

questions.title: Data lineage and permitted use
questions.prompt: Can material data sources, transformations, permissions and disposal be substantiated?
questions.evidence: Lineage, data fitness, permitted-use decisions and disposal observation.
questions.action: Trace a material data path and verify its permitted use and lifecycle treatment.

questions.title: Currency and change triggers
questions.prompt: Are evidence, models and policy versions time-bounded, with stale or changed inputs reopening review?
questions.evidence: Evidence register, review dates, version digests and a tested change-trigger review.
questions.action: Set review deadlines and test reopening after a stale record or external change signal.

questions.title: Reproducible challenge
questions.prompt: Can another reviewer reproduce the result, inspect contrary evidence and verify corrective-action closure?
questions.evidence: Reproduction instructions, independent review, failed cases and closure retest.
questions.action: Ask a separate reviewer to reproduce a sample and retain unresolved findings.

sources.title: BCG, The AI Maturity Matrix 2026
sources.role: Macroeconomic context. User-supplied 28-page PDF; original not republished.

sources.title: Fabrizio Degni, AI Maturity 2026: capacity to deploy and govern consequences
sources.role: Conceptual four-pillar proposal, retrieved from public post. PALO scoring is a new operationalization.

sources.title: PALO v3.1 Governance Control Plane
sources.role: Existing controls and evidence contracts, verified against local source.

comparison.established: BCG compares national economies through exposure and ASPIRE readiness.
comparison.newPerspective: PALO assesses a named organization, public institution or system with a defined boundary and observation window.

comparison.established: Assessment Path routes risk, impact, controls and an evidence bundle; it already includes governance.
comparison.newPerspective: A separate profile records evidence strength, currency, four governance pillars and improvement priorities.

comparison.established: BCG includes policy quality, institutional effectiveness, data governance and national AI legislation.
comparison.newPerspective: Check whether named people can challenge, revoke, observe effects and deliver remedy in practice.

comparison.established: BCG discusses strategic choices across the AI stack.
comparison.newPerspective: Exercise supplier exit, changed commitments, data permissions and accountability for inherited dependencies.

comparison.established: BCG recognises wider exposure as systems act in the physical economy.
comparison.newPerspective: Test bounded authority, revocation, cumulative impact and authoritative post-state observation.

comparison.established: A readiness snapshot and existing evidence routing identify a starting point.
comparison.newPerspective: Expired or incomplete evidence remains unresolved; comparable scoped reassessments show ordinal progress.
